lead: Low-cost houses from 1929, with rustic roofs and gardens: the smallest neighbourhood in Barcelona.
text: Between 1929 and 1932, 534 houses were built here for workers who lived in shacks on Montjuïc, coinciding with the International Exposition. Its name comes from the Can Peguera farmhouse (masia), known for making glue from the resin of the nearby pine wood, and for many years the neighbourhood was called Ramón Albó.

At 0.12 km², it is the smallest neighbourhood in Barcelona, and it is also the best preserved of the four groups of casas baratas (low-cost houses), because its own residents have kept improving them. Its streets are lined with single-storey family houses, with rustic roofs and small front gardens, and its only square, Plaça de Sant Francesc Xavier, is laid out around the former chapel of the farmhouse.
housing: Single-storey family houses with front gardens, alongside a few social housing blocks.
